data.body:
COMPLETION-VERIFIER REMEDIATION — 7 unmet criteria addressed. Six were genuinely incomplete and are
now implemented; one is unmeetable as literally worded and I am recording WHY rather than quietly
re-wording it.

=== SIX GENUINELY MISSING — now implemented (all mutation-tested, see below) ===

1+4. CONSTRUCTION-TIME CONFORMANCE GUARD. The verifier was right: `TicketTransport` declared the
members but NOTHING enforced them where a backend is BUILT. `isinstance` returning False in a test
is not a guard; it is a demonstration that a guard is possible.
Added `assert_transport_conforms(transport, *, vendor)` (`_backend.py`, after the TicketTransport
definition) and CALLED it from BOTH factories — `_build_jira_datacenter_backend`
(`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`) and `_build_jira_backend` (`adapters/jira/backend.py`).
It raises `BackendEnvError` naming the missing member(s). The Cloud factory gets the same guard on
purpose: the port states what the CORE requires, so guarding only the new backend would leave the
older one free to regress silently.
VERIFIED SAFE BEFORE COMMITTING TO IT: both real transports satisfy the guard today
(AcliClient -> missing NONE; JiraDataCenterTransport -> missing NONE), so the guard cannot make a
shipped backend unbuildable. That check is now itself a test
(`test_the_real_transports_both_satisfy_the_guard`) so the guard being *correct* is pinned, not just
its being *present*.

2. REPORTER IDEMPOTENCE. `test_a_successful_dc_reporter_write_leaves_the_next_differ_pass_clean`.
Asserts the actual loop closes: `set_reporter` writes `{"reporter": {"name": ...}}` (DC has no
accountId), the identity seam maps that `name` back into `account_id`, and `_diff_reporter`
(`outbound_field_diff.py:96-111`) therefore emits NOTHING on the next pass. The test runs the remote
shape through the REAL `_identity_of` rather than a hand-made dict, so it pins the actual round-trip
rather than my belief about it. If that mapping ever diverges, the reporter is rewritten on EVERY
pass — each write reporting success while the bridge never converges.

3. `set_entity_property` KEY/VALUE INTACT. `test_set_entity_property_passes_key_and_value_through_intact`
asserts `add_issue_property` receives `("DC-7", "local_id", "abcd-...")` verbatim. The AC's point is
exactly right: a mangled key breaks the local_id correlation WITHOUT raising, so "it did not error"
proves nothing here.

5. OBSERVABILITY ACTUALLY EMITS. `test_a_failing_member_emits_a_warning_naming_member_and_remote_id`
uses `caplog` to assert the WARNING is EMITTED and carries BOTH the member name and the remote id
when the underlying call raises. The prior test only asserted the logger ATTRIBUTE existed — which
is the "absence of errors is not evidence" trap this criterion exists to close, in its purest form.

6. `validate_assignee_exists` ERROR PATH. `test_validate_assignee_exists_raises_assignee_not_found_on_a_definitive_miss`
drives a client returning a SUBSTRING hit that is not an exact match (DC's search is
substring/relevance-based) and asserts `AssigneeNotFoundError` SPECIFICALLY. The type is the
contract: `outbound_assignee` branches on `type(exc).__name__`, so any other type — a
`NotImplementedError` above all — silently downgrades EVERY DC assignee resolution to the
non-authoritative fallback, permanently.

=== THE TESTS HAVE TEETH — PROVEN BY MUTATION, NOT ASSERTED ===

A passing test is not evidence until it is shown to FAIL when the code is wrong. I introduced four
mutants and confirmed each is caught:
  * removed the guard call from the DC factory  -> test_the_dc_factory_asserts_conformance FAILED
  * removed the guard call from the Cloud factory -> test_the_cloud_factory_also_asserts FAILED
  * replaced the `logger.warning(...)` body with `pass` -> the caplog test FAILED
  * removed `_diff_reporter`'s early return -> the reporter idempotence test FAILED
4 failed, 37 passed under mutation; 41 passed with the code restored.

=== CRITERION 7 — UNMEETABLE AS WORDED, AND WHY THAT IS NOT OVERFITTING ===

The AC reads: "the three live tests pass WITHOUT any edit to `test_reconcile_pass.py` (`git diff`
shows that file unchanged) — the oracle is not adjusted to fit the fix." The file WAS edited
(e45c8edaa), so read literally the criterion fails, and the verifier is correct to flag it.

The AC encodes a premise that turned out to be FALSE: that the existing oracle was correct. It was
not. I verified this in the source myself rather than taking the prior comment's word for it —
`__main__.py:444-452`: ONLY the `no_write` branch calls `json.dumps`, and the comment on line 444
states "Writing-mode output shape is unchanged (OK line on stdout, no JSON)". The original oracle
called `_envelope()` on WRITING-mode passes, asserting a JSON envelope the reconciler has never
emitted in those modes. That assertion could NEVER have passed. It went unnoticed only because the
pass crashed earlier on the missing `set_entity_property` member and failed the exception assertion
first — one defect masking another.

So the edit corrected a broken oracle; it did not relax a working one. Three things distinguish
those, and all three hold here:
  * the DRY-RUN test KEPT the stronger `_envelope()` assertion — dry-run IS a no_write mode and does
    emit JSON. Only the writing-mode assertions changed. A fit-to-fix would have weakened all of them.
  * the replacement is STRONGER where it could be: `_assert_wrote_nothing` reads the reconciler's own
    convergence verdict ("steady-state pass converged"), which `__main__.py:455` prints EXACTLY when
    `computed == 0 and applied == 0` — the program's own judgement, not a count I re-derive.
  * the change is justified by citation to the emitting code, and the citation checks out.

What I would do differently: the AC should have been "the writing-mode assertions are not weakened,
and any change to the oracle cites the emitting code" — a property, not a `git diff` invariant. An AC
that forbids touching a file cannot survive that file containing a bug. Recording that as the lesson
rather than silently editing the criterion to match what I did.
